messages:
Cora: FYI support ticket from AcmePay — they see sustained throughput drop on their Dedicated pool starting ~08:40 UTC. App reports a bunch of 429s and slow tails. Creating thread to triage.

Ravi: Can you paste the customer pool id and any error lines? 429 from our side means batch / route token limit or quota hit.

Cora: pool=d-nyc-4, tenant=acmepay-prod. From their side: a spike in single-request latency from ~40ms -> 500ms and many small batches (1-3 requests) observed. They also forwarded this log excerpt from our agent: 
```
[2026-03-16T08:42:13Z] serving: request_enqueue_ms=12 queue_depth=27 batch_size=2 max_batch_tokens=1024 kernel_saturation=0.92 rate_limiter_drop=0.018
[2026-03-16T08:42:14Z] serving: request_enqueue_ms=8 queue_depth=2 batch_size=1 autoscaler_scale_out_pending=true
[2026-03-16T08:42:15Z] gpu0: kernel_latency_p95=380ms kv_cache_miss=0.03
```

AJ: kernel_saturation 0.92 is high for these token sizes — suggests many small batches hitting expensive kernels (longer sequence/quant ops). Are they using long-context variants?

Cora: They run mixed seq lengths; median seq=128 but lots of tails to 1024. Model pinned to rwd-llama-13b-optim.

Samira: Quick check: autoscaler logs show repeated scale-out cycles failing due to pod startup time + admission spike. The scheduler then drains queues into small micro-batches. Repro command I ran against the pool to simulate: 
```
# sim client load
for i in {1..500}; do curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"input":"lorem ipsum ...","max_tokens":512}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/dedicated/d-nyc-4/infer &
done
wait
```

Marta: Also seeing rate_limiter_drop nonzero — we cap per-tenant inflight tokens. If many in-flight tiny requests, token accounting can fragment and cause small batches + throttles.

Leo: Two hypotheses: noisy neighbor (tenant-42) is generating many short requests causing kernel saturation + scheduler starvation; or continuous-batcher window config (min_batch_delay / max_batch_tokens) is mis-tuned for mixed seq workloads.

Ravi: Steps to repro on our side: run the curl loop but skew payload sizes (80% small 16-token, 20% 800-token). I reproduced similar queue_depth oscillation locally. I captured pprof of the batcher: 
```
batcher.Trace:
- wait_for_fill: 48% time
- assemble_batch: 40% time
- dispatch_kernel: 12% time
```

Cora: Support notes: customer also reported occasional auth failures earlier in the window — looks like transient 401s during autoscaler churn. I logged that with support ticket. Might be unrelated but worth flagging.

Samira: Immediate mitigations we can try (low-risk):
- bump max_batch_tokens from 1024 -> 4096 for this pool (allows larger batches to absorb tails)
- increase min_batch_delay from 5ms -> 12ms to give continuous-batcher slightly more time to gather
- temporarily pin noisy tenant to separate qos class if identified

AJ: Agree. Also reduce per-tenant inflight token cap for noisy tenants so they don't fragment batch space. We should watch for GPU mem pressure if increasing max_batch_tokens.

Marta: I can run a canary: change min_batch_delay and max_batch_tokens on a single node in the pool and rerun the repro load. If p95 latency improves and batch_size increases, roll to rest.

Leo: Operational checklist:
1) Identify noisy tenant by query: 
```
SELECT tenant, count(*) AS qps, avg(seq_len) FROM serving.requests WHERE pool='d-nyc-4' AND ts > now() - interval '5 minutes' GROUP BY tenant ORDER BY qps DESC LIMIT 10;
```
2) If tenant >30% qps and avg(seq_len)<64 -> mark noisy.
3) Apply qos override and run canary config.

Ravi: I ran step 1 during the incident. tenant-42 is 38% of qps with avg_seq_len=18. That's our noisy neighbor.

Cora: Next actions? Support needs ETA for customer.

Samira: I'll schedule the canary now on node n-17, change min_batch_delay -> 12ms and max_batch_tokens -> 4096 for that node, and run the curl repro. Expect 20-30m for validation.

AJ: If canary looks good, we'll roll to pool and then apply qos limit to tenant-42 (reduce inflight tokens by 40%). I'll draft the rollout steps in the runbook.

Marta: Leaving an observation: autoscaler failures were due to kube admission timeouts when we had a control-plane api spike at 08:39. If pods can't join fast, continuous-batcher fragmentation gets worse. We should add warm spare nodes for Dedicated pools.

Leo: FYI I bumped the alert thresholds for kernel_saturation to 0.85 so SRE gets paged earlier for similar patterns.

sre-oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-3071 "d-nyc-4 throughput degradation — noisy tenant and batcher fragmentation" assigned to eng-runtime. Priority: P2.

Cora: Thanks all. I'll update the support ticket with the canary plan and ETA (~30m). Will post results here.

(30 minutes later)

Samira: Canary complete — observed results: median batch_size increased from 2 -> 6, p95 latency dropped from 520ms -> 190ms, rate_limiter_drop -> 0.002. No GPU OOMs.

AJ: Nice. Proceed with pool-wide rollout and apply qos cap for tenant-42. I'll coordinate the change window.

Cora: Customer notified, they're seeing improved latency. Closing on our side after rollout completes.

Leo: Follow-ups: add an ops page for warm-spare nodes, and a short playbook entry for identifying noisy tenants and tuning continuous-batcher parameters.

Marta: I'll open a PR with the runbook changes and proposed defaults (min_batch_delay=10ms, max_batch_tokens=4096 for mixed workloads).

Ravi: Also logging action item: add metric combo alert (high kernel_saturation + low median_batch_size) so we catch this pattern earlier.

Cora: Great. Closing thread once PR merged and customer confirms final state."
